sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
The framed block is a white 7×12 with a gray border (the border is rows 24 and 32, columns 25 and 38). So the block including the border is 9×14.
Let me completely rethink the game. Elements:
1. Top-left legend: white 5×10 on top of purple 5×10.
2. Top-right: two color swatches (white, purple) with a selection underline.
3. Play field: framed white block 7×12 (with gray border), white block 10×10 below it.
4. Bottom: shrinking timer bar.
5. Controls: LEFT/RIGHT rotate the framed block by 45°; SPACE paints the lower block with the framed block's color (depth = framed height − gap, width = overlap); MOUSE selects a color swatch (or clicks a block).
Hmm, wait. Actually, maybe the framed block is a "cursor/selection frame" that can be moved and rotated, and it indicates which region of the lower block will be painted? But the frame is on the upper block, not on the lower one.
Or, the game is: "the framed block is a piece you can rotate; SPACE drops/stamps it onto the lower block; the goal is to make the lower block match the legend."
Let me think about the legend again: white 5×10 + purple 5×10 stacked vertically = a 10×10 block split horizontally: top half white, bottom half purple. The lower block is 10×10! So the goal is probably: make the lower 10×10 block = top 5 rows white, bottom 5 rows purple.
Currently the lower block is all white. So I need to paint the bottom 5 rows of the lower block purple!
But SPACE paints from the top of the lower block (the side facing the framed block). To paint the bottom 5 rows, the framed block would need to be below the lower block. Can I move the framed block down? UP/DOWN didn't work…
Wait, maybe UP/DOWN moves the framed block, but the frame is currently in the "up" position and… no, that's not it. Let me test more carefully: maybe the framed block can be moved with the arrow keys, but it rotates instead? No, LEFT/RIGHT rotated it.
Hmm, or maybe the paint is applied to the lower block on the side opposite the framed block? No — the first SPACE painted rows 34–38 (the top of the lower block, the side facing the framed block).
Or, the selection color matters, and SPACE paints the selected color onto the lower block on the side away from the framed block? First SPACE: purple selected, painted the top 5 rows purple. The side facing the frame. Second: white selected, painted the top 5 rows white (the purple part). The side facing the frame. Third: purple selected, the lower block is all white, nothing painted. Consistent: SPACE paints the framed block's color (or the selected color — at the time of the first SPACE the frame was purple and the selection was also purple, so ambiguous) onto the top 5 rows of the lower block.
Actually, at the time of the second SPACE: the frame was white, the selection was white. Third: the frame was white, the selection was purple → nothing painted (the lower block is already white; painting white on white = no visible change, but board_changed was True — hmm, that might just be the timer bar).
So I still can't distinguish between "the frame's color" and "the selected color." Test: select purple (already selected), frame is white, lower block is white → SPACE painted nothing visible. To distinguish: I need a case where the frame's color ≠ the selected color and the lower block has a different color. For example, paint the top 5 rows of the lower block purple (select purple, frame white → SPACE). If the top 5 rows become purple → the selected color is used. If nothing happens → the frame's color is used.
Current state: selection = purple, frame = white, lower block = all white. So: SPACE now. If the top 5 rows of the lower block become purple → the selected color is what's used.
Let's do it.
